title: Japan-listed Remixpoint liquidates all altcoin holdings, consolidates portfolio to bitcoin-only strategy
dek: Remixpoint, a Japan-listed treasury company, sold all positions in ETH, SOL, XRP, and DOGE on September 1, 2026, recording a realized gain of ¥117.77 million and consolidating its crypto strategy exclusively into bitcoin. The shift reflects management's assessment of altcoin volatility over the summer and follows only three months of diversified altcoin accumulation.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: A publicly traded Japanese firm abandoned its altcoin portfolio after three months and moved entirely to bitcoin, signaling institutional skepticism of alternative cryptocurrencies.
bottom_line: Remixpoint's three-month altcoin experiment ending in full liquidation underscores how institutional treasury strategies respond to volatile market conditions. The question is whether this move reflects a company-specific risk reassessment or signals broader institutional confidence shifting away from altcoins toward bitcoin's stability.
body:
Remixpoint, a Japan-listed company, sold its entire altcoin portfolio on September 1, 2026, moving to an exclusive bitcoin strategy after managing diversified cryptocurrency holdings for just three months. The company recorded a realized gain of ¥117.77 million from the liquidation, per U.Today reporting.
The sale reflects a reversal of strategy adopted in June 2026, when Remixpoint began accumulating altcoins to hedge against the weakening yen.  By late August, management had reassessed market risks and altcoin volatility, adopting what it described as a "selection and concentration" strategy.
Remixpoint's altcoin portfolio included approximately 1.2 million XRP tokens alongside Solana and Dogecoin positions, according to U.Today. The total book value of altcoin holdings at the beginning of the period stood at ¥761.04 million. The company had accumulated these positions over a three-month window from June through August 2026.
Between February and August 2026, the firm accumulated 14.92 BTC in interest from a bitcoin lending program, generating ¥164.21 million in additional returns, per U.Today's reporting.
According to U.Today, the gain from altcoin sales will be recognized as business-division revenue in the second quarter of fiscal 2027.
The shift demonstrates institutional skepticism about alternative cryptocurrencies during a period of elevated market volatility. Bitcoin's utility in Remixpoint's lending arrangements, combined with its lower volatility profile compared to altcoins over the summer months, appears to have informed the concentrated allocation decision.
